style: glossy stylised game art, clean bold edges, neon night-construction palette, soft rim light, 3D-ish render, never a photo
notes: A neon night construction site: a tower of glowing modules stacked against a dark indigo skyline. Five sprites carry a nine-slice border in their .meta (sprite_module_core, sprite_module_accent, sprite_module_gold, sprite_base_plinth, sprite_hud_strip), so their prompts ask for a uniform rim and a flat, quiet centre that survives being stretched to any width - the module width really does change every time the player cuts the tower. A nine-slice border is only valid while BOTH fixed edges fit inside the drawn size: a module is 42px tall on screen, so its vertical border must stay well under 21px per edge or Unity renders the slab as a sliver. The two skyline sprites and sprite_segment_fill carry no border and are stretched whole, so their art must FILL its canvas and match the aspect written into the scene (1024x384 and 128x64) - a square icon-shaped render there becomes a giant rounded square across the play field. Direction is declared explicitly only where the code never mirrors the art: sprite_wind_arrow points RIGHT and sprite_icon_back points LEFT; everything else is symmetric and must not be mirrored. Sprite prompts do not argue about the backdrop colour because the pipeline cuts the background away. No prompt contains the app name and no sprite carries lettering of any kind - splash and menu branding is the abstract mark (sprite_mark_badge) plus stacked modules, never a word.
